source_evidence.observation: ExecutionLineage and ExecutionTransition bind causal_id + generation + request_id, plus later admission/execution/verification identities, but do not carry the canonical session_id + agent_id + task_id + turn_id CausalIdentity tuple and do not carry invocation_id/tool_use_id/effect_id.

The current WP-102 survivor already carries full parent/child CausalIdentity and explicit invocation_id + tool_use_id + delegation_id, demonstrating that those dimensions exist immediately upstream of the WP-105 execution/completion boundary.

The earlier Stage-1 review already identified omitted causal context and generation-domain ambiguity as a projection-collapse class. Current WP-102 source has since fused the full parent/child identity into its binding preimage, but WP-105 still exposes a narrower execution projection.

The Triggerword-4 donor branch contains a deterministic call-scoped result re-entry guard whose explicit purpose is preventing mutable session-scoped routing from attaching one interleaved call's result to another call.

The donor regression constructs two calls in one session with the same result digest and requires mismatched observed/target invocation identity to fail before store mutation. This is source/component evidence only and does not supply Frankenstein-2.0 runtime credit.

hypotheses: If two admissible Stage-1 execution lineages can share causal_id + causal generation + request_id while differing in canonical session/agent/task/turn context, the current WP-105 projection cannot distinguish them and can accept a transition against the wrong semantic context.

Even when causal_id is unique, a later adapter that maps call-scoped tool/effect observations into WP-105 using session/current-row state rather than an explicit invocation/tool-use binding can reintroduce cross-talk between overlapping calls. Equal result digests are insufficient to detect that error.
counterhypotheses: A mechanically enforced upstream invariant may make the tuple (causal_id, generation, request_id) globally unique and may bind every WP-105 transition to the exact WP-102 invocation/tool-use identity before admission. If executable tests prove that boundary, expanding WP-105 itself may be unnecessary.

WP-105 may intentionally remain a narrow generic state machine while a separate typed adapter owns canonical CausalIdentity plus invocation/tool-use/effect correlation. If so, that adapter must be explicit, fail closed, and executable; implicit session routing is not sufficient.

requirements: Construct two distinct canonical CausalIdentity contexts in the same session with different task_id/turn_id and distinct invocation_id/tool_use_id.
Drive both through the same execution/completion adapter with deliberately equal result digests.
Attempt to apply call-B's observed result/effect identity to call-A's execution lineage.
Require rejection before any persistence/effect/completion mutation and prove call-A remains unchanged.
Require exact call-A -> call-A and call-B -> call-B replay to remain deterministic/idempotent.
Bind the test to exact source blobs and preserve source-only scope while GitHub Actions remains in the current zero-step pre-admission failure class.
cheapest_high_information_discriminator.promotion_condition: Either prove an executable uniqueness/adapter invariant that makes the collision inadmissible, or add an explicit typed CausalIdentity + invocation/tool-use/effect correlation boundary before WP-105 transitions can mutate execution/completion state.

non_overlap_decision: DO_NOT_MODIFY_ACTIVE_WP105_OWNER_SOURCE_IN_THIS_REVIEW. Record the falsifier only. The existing Triggerword-4 effect-invocation primitive is treated as donor evidence rather than duplicated implementation.
